walkthroughs.body_html:
Metals & Reactivity Series — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Metals & Reactivity Series brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Metals & Reactivity Series.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which metal will displace copper from copper sulfate?
options: Gold
Silver
Iron
Mercury

mcqs.q: Sodium is stored under oil because:
options: it dissolves in air
it reacts vigorously with water and oxygen
it explodes spontaneously
it rusts

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: The system shifts to amplify the change because reactions always proceed in the disturbed direction.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.
In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.

mcqs.q: Does a catalyst affect the position of equilibrium?
options: A catalyst increases the yield by being consumed in the forward reaction only.
The system shifts to amplify the change because reactions always proceed in the disturbed direction.
A catalyst shifts the equilibrium towards the products.
No — it speeds up both the forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but at the same position.

mcqs.q: When a stress shifts an equilibrium, does the system fully undo the change?
options: The system shifts to completely cancel the change and return concentrations to their original values.
No — Le Chatelier's principle says the system PARTIALLY opposes the change; equilibrium shifts to a new position that minimises but doesn't eliminate the disturbance.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
The system shifts to amplify the change because reactions always proceed in the disturbed direction.
